questions.q: The monomers of Glyptal, as given in exam answers, are:
questions.explain: Glyptal is the polyester of ethylene glycol with phthalic acid (the 1,2 or ortho acid). Terephthalic (para) acid with ethylene glycol gives Terylene, and isophthalic acid is used for neither.

questions.q: How many carbon atoms are present in the repeating unit of Terylene?
questions.explain: The repeating unit –O–CH₂–CH₂–O–CO–C₆H₄–CO– is C₁₀H₈O₄: two carbons from ethylene glycol and eight from terephthalic acid.

questions.q: When dimethyl terephthalate is used instead of terephthalic acid to make Terylene, the small molecule released is:
questions.explain: Dimethyl terephthalate reacts with ethylene glycol by transesterification, so methanol is lost instead of water.

questions.q: Which statement correctly explains why Terylene is a fibre while Glyptal is used as a coating resin?
options: Terylene is an addition polymer, Glyptal a condensation polymer
The 1,4-acid in Terylene continues the chain in a straight line so chains pack regularly; the 1,2-acid in Glyptal turns the chain sharply
Terylene contains amide links that hydrogen-bond, Glyptal contains only ester links
Glyptal is made from ethylene glycol, which cannot form long chains
questions.explain: Both are polyesters (condensation polymers). The para geometry of terephthalic acid gives straight, regular chains that line up into a semicrystalline fibre, while the ortho acid kinks the chain.
